name: Build Approved Reels
description: Cuts every APPROVED moment in the reel plan onto its own Resolve timeline, bad takes removed, captions rendered through steps 4.01 and 4.05.

inputs.name: project_folder
inputs.description: Absolute path to the project. Whitelisted global injected by gather_step_inputs. The plan, the transcript and the Resolve binding are all read relative to it.

inputs.name: timeline_transcript
inputs.description: The master timeline's speech, REBUILT from source by `python3 -m library.tools.timeline_transcript <project> --write`. NO STEP PRODUCES IT - it needs Resolve open and WhisperX loaded - so it has no producing edge and reaches this step because the manifest declares it. Declaring it required is what derives requirements.timeline_transcript.on_file for this node.

inputs.name: skip_captions
inputs.description: Build the timelines without rendering subtitle overlays. The `--skip-captions` flag of `manage_project.py build-reels`, which exists because the Remotion render is the expensive half and a structural check does not need it.

inputs.name: only_reels
inputs.description: Reel NUMBERS to build. Absent means every approved moment, which is what every build did before. The `--only-reel` flag of `manage_project.py build-reels`. It exists because the delete step now removes only the names this call will place, so building one reel is a real operation rather than a full rebuild that happens to place one timeline.

inputs.name: timeline_name_suffix
inputs.description: Appended to the Resolve timeline name each reel is built INTO, and to the `timeline` component of every caption filename so the overlays cannot overwrite another timeline's. Absent means the plan's own name, which REPLACES the existing timeline of that name. The `--name-suffix` flag of `manage_project.py build-reels`.

outputs.name: reel_build
outputs.description: What was PLACED: the timelines built, the plan they were built from, the caption content hashes recorded at build time, and the Resolve names built into. Carried by the edge to verify_reels so the verifier grades the same answer the build wrote. Also carries what the build was ASKED for - `reels_requested` and `name_suffix` - so a record of one reel built into a new container does not read as a full rebuild that placed one timeline.

metadata.author: prajwal
metadata.notes: Belongs to library/processes/reels, not to edit_video. See docs/REEL_BUILD_HAS_NO_OWNING_NODE.md for the measurement that says why a reel build cannot be a node of the edit_video DAG.
